source_fact_map.source_excerpt:
The UK's Foreign Office investigates Robert Maxwell & Russia (September 1, 1949)

The Trump Timeline:

September 1, 1949

Shortly after the end of World War II in September 1945, Robert Maxwell (born Ján Ludvík Hyman Binyamin Hoch) was transferred from the British Army to the Berlin headquarters of the UK’s Foreign Office (FO). It’s not long before the FO suspects there is a problem with him and launches an investigation (exact date unknown).

Reports of Maxwell’s suspicious activity and ties to foreign intelligence agencies begin hitting the FO’s covert Information Research Department (IRD) by the end of 1949, if not years earlier. At the time of this writing, there is not a clear timeline of the investigations, which the department files under “Captain Ian Maxwell.”

corrected_proposal_for_survivor.title: Trump Reinstates Schedule F as Schedule Policy/Career
corrected_proposal_for_survivor.description_short: Trump's January 20, 2025 executive order reinstated Schedule F under the name Schedule Policy/Career.
corrected_proposal_for_survivor.description_medium: On January 20, 2025, Donald Trump signed an executive order immediately reinstating the 2020 Schedule F order and renaming the category “Schedule Policy/Career.” The order directed the Office of Personnel Management to amend regulations and issue guidance on additional positions for agencies to consider. It establishes a federal workforce policy directive; it does not show how many employees were later reclassified or removed.
corrected_proposal_for_survivor.description_long: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump signed “Restoring Accountability to Policy-Influencing Positions Within the Federal Workforce.” Section 2 immediately reinstated Executive Order 13957, the 2020 order creating Schedule F, subject to amendments in the new order. Those amendments replaced the excepted-service schedule label “F” with “Policy/Career” and directed the Office of Personnel Management to amend regulations that could impede implementation. The order also directed OPM to issue, within 30 days, guidance about additional position categories agencies should consider recommending for inclusion. It says employees in or applicants for these positions need not personally or politically support the President, but are required to faithfully implement administration policies; failure to do so is grounds for dismissal. These are the signed order’s rules and directions. The accessed document does not establish how many positions were later reclassified, how many employees lost protections, or whether any specific person was dismissed under it. This record describes the enacted policy mechanism, not a completed workforce purge or an asserted list of political enemies.
